h1: The 4 Best Toro Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Toro Leaf Blowers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: four Toro leaf blowers, from 60V cordless brushless models to a corded vacuum mulcher, with airflow figures and tradeoffs.
summary: The Toro 60V Max brushless model at 605 CFM and 120 MPH is the best Toro blower for most yards. The Flex Force gives 565 CFM for owners of that platform. A second 605 CFM model drops to 115 MPH and the lowest cordless price tier. The Ultra 12 amp is the vacuum and mulcher choice.
intro: Toro makes blowers for two very different jobs, and mixing them up is the common mistake. The cordless 60V Max models are for clearing leaves quickly with no cable to drag. The corded Ultra is closer to a leaf vacuum that also mulches, and it trades the freedom of a battery for a different purpose.

Four Toro models made this ranking. Our editors compared them from listed specifications: airflow, speed, battery platform and function. When a listing gave no airflow or runtime figure, we left it out rather than guess, so some comparisons rely on tier and function.

products.name: Toro 60-Volt Max Electric Brushless Cordless Leaf Blower with 120 MPH
products.verdict: 605 CFM and 120 MPH from a brushless cordless 60V Max platform.
products.description:
This Toro runs on the 60V Max platform with a brushless motor, and it lists 605 CFM of airflow and 120 MPH. It is fully cordless, so there is no cable to manage, and it is priced in the $100 to $200 tier.

It takes first place by pairing the highest Toro airflow with the fastest air in a cordless body. The corded Ultra cannot match its freedom of movement. The Flex Force below it lists 565 CFM, roughly 40 CFM less, in the same price tier.

Choose it for a typical yard that needs a capable cordless blower. The honest caveat is that the $100 to $200 tier is not the cheapest way to get 605 CFM from Toro, because another model below it undercuts it, and runtime is not listed.
products.idealFor: Typical yards that want cordless power.

products.name: Toro Flex Force 60-Volt Max Brushless and Cordless Leaf Blower
products.verdict: 565 CFM on the Flex Force 60V Max brushless platform.
products.description:
The Toro Flex Force is a 60V Max brushless cordless blower listing 565 CFM of airflow. It sits in the $100 to $200 tier, matching the top pick's price.

It ranks second because the airflow is lower by 40 CFM for the same money, and no speed figure appears in the listing. The Flex Force name matters more as a battery ecosystem than as a performance claim, so it beats the others mainly for people who already own that line.

Buy it if you have Flex Force batteries and tools and want to share them. Skip it if you are starting from scratch, since the lead pick lists more airflow at the same price. The caveat is the lower airflow and a missing MPH listing, which makes direct comparison harder.

products.name: Toro 115 MPH 605 CFM 60-Volt Max Lithium-Ion Brushless Cordless Leaf Blower
products.verdict: 605 CFM and 115 MPH in the $50 to $100 tier.
products.description:
This Toro lists 605 CFM and 115 MPH from a 60V Max lithium-ion brushless cordless design. It is the cheapest cordless Toro here, with a $50 to $100 price tag.

Third place follows because the speed is 5 MPH below the top pick, a small gap that matters mostly for wet or stuck leaves. The airflow matches the top model, and the price tier is lower, which makes it a sensible value buy.

Buy it if you want the same 605 CFM at a lower cost and can live with slightly less speed. Skip it if you want the 120 MPH figure. The honest caveat is that battery details are not given in the listing, so check what comes in the box and how long it runs before you commit.

products.name: Toro 51609 Ultra 12 amp Variable-Speed Electric Blower
products.verdict: A 12 amp variable-speed electric that also vacuums and mulches.
products.description:
The Toro 51609 Ultra is a 12 amp variable speed electric blower listed as a vacuum and mulcher, with a speed figure up to 235. It falls in the $200 to $500 tier, the highest in this ranking.

It ranks fourth because it is a different tool. The listing gives no CFM, it needs a power source rather than a battery, and it costs the most. For people who want to shred leaves into smaller pieces, however, none of the cordless models can do that.

Buy it if you bag leaves or want mulch for beds. Skip it if cordless freedom matters or you simply want to push leaves across the lawn. The caveat is that it ties you to an electrical supply, which limits range in a larger yard.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want to mulch leaves.

whatMatters.detail: CFM, or cubic feet per minute, is the volume of air the blower moves. It decides how quickly a pile of leaves clears. The 605 CFM Toro models list more than the 565 CFM Flex Force. Find the number in the listing title, and compare it only against similar blower types.

Wind speed, in MPH, is how fast the air leaves the nozzle. It helps lift wet or stuck leaves. The top Toro lists 120 MPH and the value model 115 MPH. Compare MPH with CFM instead of relying on one number, and check the title for both.

Cordless versus corded decides how you work. Cordless blowers like the 60V Max Toro give freedom from a cable but depend on battery charge, while corded ones run as long as they are plugged in. Check the power type and whether a battery and charger are included.

A brushless motor is described as more efficient than a brushed one, with less wear. It matters for runtime and durability on battery tools. Look for the word brushless in the title, as on the three cordless models, and ignore it as a sign of power on its own.

Vacuum and mulcher function means the machine can suck up leaves and shred them to reduce volume. It only matters if you bag or compost leaves. Check for vacuum or mulcher in the title, as on the Ultra, and note that it is a different tool from the cordless blowers.

faq.a: Three of the four here are cordless: the 120 MPH 60V Max, the Flex Force, and the 115 MPH 60V Max. The Ultra 51609 is a corded electric vacuum and mulcher.
Confusing the cordless blowers with the Ultra. The 605 CFM models move leaves across the lawn, while the Ultra is a vacuum and mulcher with no CFM listed. Decide first whether you need to mulch.

faq.q: Is the 120 MPH Toro worth it over the 115 MPH one?
faq.a: It lists 5 more MPH and sits in a higher tier, $100 to $200 versus $50 to $100. Airflow is the same 605 CFM, so the 115 MPH model is the better value if speed is not critical.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Attach the nozzle and follow the maker's guide for the battery, since the listings do not detail the steps. The Ultra needs a nearby power supply instead of a battery.
Clear debris from the intake after use and store the battery as the manual directs. Keep the Flex Force and other 60V Max tools out of extreme heat, which is hard on lithium-ion packs.
Yes. The Ultra is listed as a vacuum and mulcher, which is its reason for existing. The cordless 60V Max models are blowers, so they do not shred leaves.

finalTake: Choose the 120 MPH Toro 60V Max if you want the strongest cordless blower in the range. The Flex Force suits owners of that battery system, and the 115 MPH version keeps the same airflow for less. Buy the Ultra only if mulching is the goal, since it is a corded electric rather than a battery model.
